launch.note: The one home of every per-role launch setting. A role's structured fields are the settings; launch.templates is only the wiring each agent's command follows, and the reader in scripts/paths.sh (pp_route, pp_review, pp_argv) fills its placeholders and fails before any launch on a malformed entry. A model is a family name, never a version: Claude Code resolves opus, sonnet, haiku and fable itself, and builder-codex-pass.sh resolves a Codex family to the newest model the account lists. A null effort is omitted from the command, never defaulted. fast renders as Codex service_tier=fast or Claude --settings {"fastMode":true}; false is the default tier, and the Codex review role takes it from set-up's saved answer only. A headless role (headless: true) is one a script runs with codex exec or claude -p. Every pane role is unboxed: the plugin ships no pane box, so launch.paneBox is not set.

orchestrator.note: Orchestration only; never implements. Plans with the owner, launches Builders, merges.

builder.note: One pane per batch in its own worktree; builds, runs its own Explore subagents (haiku) and review passes (builder-codex-pass.sh, model from roles.codex-reviewer), hands back a branch. Launched by builder-launch.sh.

codex-reviewer.note: The Codex review pass of the Claude+OpenAI profile. Fast mode is not set here: it changes what a run costs, so it is the owner's answer at set-up (codexFast in the project's .claude/commandeck.json, off by default). With a yes the pass preflight needs service_tier = "fast" in the Codex config.

claude-reviewer.note: The review pass of the Claude-only profile: a headless read-only session on a different family than the Builder's, so the review is not the Builder checking itself.

design-coauthor.note: The design check of a batch marked risky: builder-launch.sh --risky opens this pane before the Builder, and it writes the design note the Builder reads first. It writes that note and no code.

review-limits.note: Per Codex review. calls: model calls one review session may make. diffLines: added plus deleted lines in main...HEAD, generated files excluded; a bigger unit is split before review.

seat-liveness.note: read-verdict.sh --state: a seat's background command older than this counts as overdue, not busy, so a hung command cannot hold its driver past the stall line.
